title: Left derived functor of an exact functor
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be as in [def-sfb-left-derived-functor], and let
$F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an exact functor (exact functors preserve K-flat
quasi-isomorphisms). Then there is a canonical isomorphism $LF\cong D(F)$ with the
termwise functor $D(F)$.

proof.text: Exactness here means additivity and preservation of finite limits and finite colimits, as in [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Its final assertion gives preservation of quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. All the ambient hypotheses of [def-sfb-left-derived-functor] are assumed in the item, so that node supplies $LF:D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$ and its counit $\epsilon:LF\circ Q_{\mathcal C}\Rightarrow Q_{\mathcal D}\circ K(F)$ on $K(\mathcal C)$. Here $Q$ denotes homotopy-category localization and $K(F)$ denotes termwise application on homotopy classes.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: preservation and existence of LF

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] for the assertion that the termwise complex functor $C(F)$ preserves every quasi-isomorphism, not merely those between K-flat complexes. It also induces $K(F):K(\mathcal C)\to K(\mathcal D)$: a chain homotopy $f-g=dh+hd$ is sent to $F(f)-F(g)=F(d)F(h)+F(h)F(d)$ by additivity and preservation of composition. Thus homotopic maps have homotopic images, and identities and composition descend. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Q_{\mathcal D}$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms and $Q_{\mathcal C}:K(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal C)$ localizes at their images. Consequently $T=Q_{\mathcal D}\circ K(F)$ inverts that class of arrows.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, proof: exact functors transform quasi-isomorphisms into quasi-isomorphisms; termwise chain-homotopy calculation supplied here

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to $Q_{\mathcal C}$ and $T$. It gives $D(F):D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$ with a natural isomorphism $\varphi:D(F)\circ Q_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{\sim}T$. This is the termwise derived functor: on every complex $K$, its value at $Q_{\mathcal C}K$ is represented by $F(K)$, and clause (2) makes any two such factorizations uniquely isomorphic compatibly with $\varphi$. Use $\varphi$ itself as the counit, in the direction $D(F)Q_{\mathcal C}\Rightarrow Q_{\mathcal D}K(F)$. Thus the isomorphism written in the opposite direction in the blueprint is inverted before using it as a counit.

source.place: Proof, second and third sentences: termwise factorization and the direction of its counit

proof.text: Every component of $\varphi$ is invertible, hence so is its component at every K-flat complex. Apply the converse characterization in [def-sfb-left-derived-functor], for the same additive $F$ and the preservation property already established in step 1. It follows that $(D(F),\varphi)$ is a total left derived functor of $T$ along $Q_{\mathcal C}$. No assertion that $F$ sends K-flat objects to K-flat objects is needed, and no monoidal structure on $\mathcal D$ is used.

source.place: Proof, fourth sentence: characterization by the counit on K-flat complexes

proof.text: The two total left derived pairs $(LF,\epsilon)$ from [def-sfb-left-derived-functor] and $(D(F),\varphi)$ from step 4 are right Kan extensions of the same $T$ along the same $Q_{\mathcal C}$. Apply [lem-sfb-right-kan-extension-unique-iso] with $R=LF$ and $S=D(F)$. It gives the unique natural isomorphism $u:LF\xrightarrow{\sim}D(F)$ satisfying $\varphi\circ(uQ_{\mathcal C})=\epsilon$, and its inverse satisfies $\epsilon\circ(u^{-1}Q_{\mathcal C})=\varphi$. This counit compatibility specifies the claimed canonical comparison, rather than making an arbitrary choice of isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: unique counit-compatible comparison

proof_origin.place: Proof, all five sentences; preservation and localization expanded using Stacks Tag 015F and the existing localization and Kan-uniqueness nodes
